question: What is the main job of a health Information Retrieval System (IRS)?

options.A: To store, organize, and provide access to medical data
options.B: To monitor real-time patient vital signs
options.D: To directly diagnose complex patient pathologies

explanation: Think of an IRS like a well-organized digital library. Its main job is to help you store and quickly find the medical information you need! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h1)

question: How does an information retrieval system help you practice evidence-based nursing?

options.A: By calculating accurate patient drug dosages
options.B: By providing rapid access to peer-reviewed clinical research
options.C: By replacing the need for clinical judgment at the bedside
options.D: By automatically generating hospital staffing schedules

explanation: Spot on! When you can quickly pull up reliable research on your phone, you can easily base your daily nursing care on proven facts. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h1)

question: When you type a search term into a database, which part translates it so the system can understand it?
explanation: The query processor acts like a friendly translator—it takes the words you type and prepares them so the database can search properly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the main role of the indexing module in a search database?

options.A: Storing personal user search history securely
options.B: Analyzing documents and creating a searchable database structure
options.C: Translating user search phrases into plain language
options.D: Calculating the final relevance score for displayed articles

explanation: Indexing is like making a textbook table of contents ahead of time, so the database doesn't have to read every single word from scratch every time you search. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h2)

question: If you want to broaden your search using different medical synonyms, which Boolean operator should you use?
explanation: Use 'OR' when you want to cast a wider net! It tells the database to find articles containing any of your chosen synonyms. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h3)

question: You need articles about malaria treatment in children, but you want to leave out adult studies. Which search query works best?

options.A: malaria OR treatment OR children NOT adults
options.B: malaria AND treatment AND adults NOT children
options.C: malaria AND treatment AND children NOT adults
options.D: malaria NOT treatment AND children AND adults

explanation: Great choice! 'AND' connects your must-have topics, while 'NOT' tells the system to drop any papers focusing on adults. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h3)

question: In healthcare literature databases, what does the acronym MeSH stand for?
explanation: MeSH stands for Medical Subject Headings. It's the official keyword system used by the National Library of Medicine to organize medical topics neatly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why are controlled vocabulary terms (like MeSH) better than just typing free words when doing a thorough search?

options.A: They allow the computer to automatically write the final nursing research paper
options.B: They completely eliminate the need to use Boolean operators like AND and OR
options.C: They group various synonyms and alternative spellings under a single official term
options.D: They guarantee that only free full-text articles appear in the final results

explanation: Spot on! Different authors spell things differently or use different words. MeSH gathers all those variations under one official label so you don't miss anything good. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h4)

question: In information retrieval, what does 'precision' actually measure?

options.A: The percentage of missing documents left in the database
options.B: The speed at which the search algorithm processes a query
options.C: The total number of articles stored in the database corpus
options.D: The proportion of retrieved documents that are actually relevant

explanation: Precision is all about quality: out of all the search results popping up on your screen, how many are actually useful to your topic? [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h5)

question: What happens to your search 'recall' when you broaden your search to catch every possible article?
explanation: You got it! Broadening your search means you pull in more of the total relevant documents out there, which increases your recall. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which regulation governs data privacy and protection within healthcare systems in Nigeria?
explanation: The NDPR is the primary legal framework that protects personal and health data privacy across Nigerian institutions. Good to know for practice! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is a major clinical danger of information overload when using poorly designed search systems?

options.A: Inability of the database to utilize Boolean operator commands
options.B: Clinician decision fatigue and potential oversight of critical care details
options.C: Permanent physical damage to hospital database server hardware
options.D: Automatic deletion of patient electronic health record histories

explanation: Exactly. Sifting through endless, messy search results drains your mental energy, which can lead to fatigue and missed details in patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h6)
